page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Running head at the top left, page number at the top right. No marginal notes. Catchword at the lower right.

main_text.l: ni sint quibus efficacia illa erroris mittatur; verum, quia
cum ejusmodi Homines ii sint, qui Veritati non
obediunt, ut ibidem Paulus ait; ii vero, qui veritati non obe-
dient, aut pessimi quidam & perversi sunt Homines,
aut ejusmodi qui nimis negligentes in Rebus divinis
sunt, quorum semper ingens fuit, & futurus est Nu-
merus; certum est, non defuturos unquam, qui ea
Punitione Dei sint digni.
§. 62. Hæc Socinus. At Inter illius Discipulos,
nemo audacius Naturæ divinæ Perfectiones violavit,
tum subtrahendo quæ ei debita erant, tum affin-
gendo quæ ei maxime incongrua erant, & eo profu-
sius indigna, quàm Conradus Vorstius, Professor
olim Theologiæ in Academia Leidensi, cujus libros
proinde, qui blasphema ista Dogmata continebant,
Seren. Rex noster Jacobus publice cremari jussit
in Cæmeterio Paulino & in utraque Academia. Inter-
cessit quoque, per legatum suum, cum fœderatis
Belgii Ordinibus, ut Illum, non solum Munere pro-
fessorio privarent, sed etiam è finibus suæ ditio-
nis pellerent. Et, ut palam ostenderet, quanto zelo
tueretur fidem antiquam & Apostolicam, cujus
ipse defensor erat, contra insana & impia Vorstii
Dogmata, edidit libellum, cui Titulum dedit,
Protestatio Antivorstia, in quo Illorum præcipua &
maxime perniciosa notavit, excerpta è variis
Ipsius Tractatibus, quorum Titulos & paginas in mar-
gine citat. Hæc autem fere sunt. Nihil vetat Deo

page.notes: Top four lines are italic and continue the paragraph from the previous page. The paragraph "§. 62." is set in roman with italic passages marked as printed; the italic run at the end of the page is marked as italic from "Nihil vetat" onward. The line "ni sint" is partly blurred, with "sint" read from context and [?] not added because the letters are legible. "De fana" in the running head is blurred; the first letter is uncertain. The final word is split as "ha-" at the line end, with "bere" as catchword. Several words in the middle of the page are smeared by print show-through and low contrast ("mittatur", "obedient", "Discipulos"); these are transcribed as best read. "Vorstii" and "Vorstius" are printed with long s rendered as s.
